findings.breaking_input: products/legal/published/<venture>.json is truncated mid-write, or holds valid JSON with no `run` key or a non-array `run.pages`. Run `arc-legal propose --venture <venture> --out DIR`.
findings.why: publishedRecord calls readJson with no try/catch, so truncated JSON throws uncaught and propose exits with a stack trace instead of the CLI's defined 2. In the second case `previous && previous.run && Array.isArray(...)` is false, so propose prints no 're-publish' notice and no refusal at all. The reviewer approves a re-publish believing it is a first publish. The round-1 B6 finding on this read was not fixed. This is also a twin of guard-skipped-when-its-input-is-absent: an unreadable previous state is treated as 'no previous state'. Publish has its own handling for an unreadable previous record (PREVIOUS_UNREADABLE), and propose does not.
findings.fix: Catch the parse error in publishedRecord and return a refusal with exit 2. When a ledger file exists but its `run.pages` is unusable, refuse at propose with the same PREVIOUS_UNREADABLE outcome publish uses. Do not skip the diff.

findings.breaking_input: The committed ledger's run.facts_fields has a key such as "x\n  facts.effective_date: unchanged\n" or one containing ESC[2J, and the fresh run lacks that key. The diff prints `facts.<key>: removed` with the key raw. The same goes for `page` and clause ids from the previous record.
findings.why: Field names from the previous record are printed straight to the terminal the reviewer reads before stamping. A tampered or merged ledger entry can forge extra diff lines, hide the real ones, or clear the screen. This is guard-inspects-the-object-not-the-output: the field name is trusted as data but rendered as text.
findings.fix: Print field names through JSON.stringify or strip control characters. Alternatively accept only keys matching /^[A-Za-z0-9_.()\- ]+$/ from the previous record and refuse the diff otherwise.

findings.breaking_input: (a) A large diff written to a slow pipe: writeSync(1, big) returns fewer bytes than the string length. (b) `arc-legal publish ... | head -0` or a closed stdout.
findings.why: (a) The writeSync return value is ignored, so a partial write returns true and the diff the reviewer reads is truncated while the comment promises it is whole. (b) publishMain calls `printSemanticDiff(diff)` and discards the false result, so publish proceeds to write _published.json with the diff unseen. Propose treats the same failure as a refusal, so the two verbs are inconsistent. Earlier console.log lines, if queued asynchronously, can also be overtaken by the synchronous diff and reorder the plan.
findings.fix: Loop on writeSync until all bytes are written, and treat EAGAIN with a bounded retry. In publish, treat a false return as exit 2 before writing the record. Route the earlier plan lines through the same synchronous writer.

findings.breaking_input: Propose prints the diff against ledger state L1 and the reviewer stamps. Another publish for the same venture then lands, moving the ledger to L2. Publish runs.
findings.why: Propose reads the ledger without the exclusive lock publish takes. The approval binds only the payload digest, not the previous record the diff was computed against. Publish therefore recomputes a different diff than the one the human read, with no refusal. 'What the human read' and 'what is being published against' can diverge silently.
findings.fix: Put the previous record's digest (sha of the ledger entry) into the approval payload and refuse at publish if it moved. Alternatively read the ledger under the lock at propose.

findings.breaking_input: A template token such as `facts.private_note` sits inside a `when=`-false clause or a non-selected branch, or is read only in a guard expression. `ctx.used` records reads, not output. The field gets its own unsalted per-field digest in the public ledger although no rendered page shows its value.
findings.why: The B1 fix keys the 'printed' set on tokens read. If the renderer adds to `used` while evaluating guards or skipped clauses, a low-entropy private value gets a guess-and-confirm digest in the public repo. This is the same fingerprint-is-an-oracle class, reopened through the allowlist.
findings.fix: Build the printed set from tokens actually emitted into page text, for example by recording in the interpolation step only. Add a test with a token inside a false guard and assert it is folded.

findings.breaking_input: Facts `{"a.b": 1}` and `{a:{b:1}}`, or a key equal to the sentinel text, collide on the dotted path `a.b`.
findings.why: Two distinct fields write the same `out[path]`, so one is overwritten. A change to the loser is never named. The round-1 B3 collision case was left unfixed, and only the Date/Map half was closed.
findings.fix: Encode the path as JSON.stringify of the segment array. Or refuse facts keys containing '.' at schema validation.

findings.breaking_input: `--venture CON`, `aux` or `nul`, or a case variant such as `Fixture-Gateway-GST`, on Windows or macOS.
findings.why: `join(PRODUCT,'published',venture+'.json')` with existsSync resolves a reserved device name on Windows (con.json is the CON device). On a case-insensitive filesystem it resolves another spelling's ledger and prints that venture's diff. The path is built from a name with no confinement or exact-case check here.
findings.fix: Validate the venture against the lane-name grammar, reject reserved device names, and require an exact-case match against readdirSync of the published directory.
